title: Make the hands good by what they serve
summary: This meets the ordinary use of hands that leaves no trace of praise. The line says hands become good when they help the Lord's praise take form.
lifeApplication: Before you type, send, build, or sign, ask what your hands are serving. Let one action today leave the Lord's praise more visible, not less.

source.shortMeaning: Hands become good when they help praise take form in the world.
source.lifeApplication: Before the next task, ask whether your hands are serving praise or vanity.

evidence.coreClaim: Hands become good when they help praise take form in the world.
evidence.turn: Let speech, sight, hands, and feet become honorable through praise.
evidence.practicalImplication: Before you type, send, build, or sign, ask what your hands are serving. Let one action today leave the Lord's praise more visible, not less.
